campus_buildings.name: Huygensgebouw

visual.height: long, mid-rise wings; sprawling low-to-mid volumes that extend across multiple courtyards with occasional taller stair cores and plant rooms breaking the roofline
unique: interior study ‘street’ with open study alcoves
fume-hood roof exhausts and screened plant visible from some angles
multiple connected wings you enter via side entrances

greenery: border hedges and pollarded trees along Toernooiveld
bikes: big bike flows at class changes
overflow bike parking near side wings and service courts
traffic: steady delivery vans to lab/service entrances
students cutting through to Mercator and Gymnasion
water: water features / ditches at Toernooiveld side (varies by area)
drainage swales near edges of the site
ground: stamped-concrete walkways with tactile strips at key doors

facilities: computing science practical spaces (some CS in Mercator)
quiet study zones along glass façades
PC halls for exams and practicals
specialized lab buildings behind Huygens (e.g., Translatorium)
sustainability: zoned ventilation for labs and offices
automated blinds and heat-gain control in long elevations
focus on re-use/renovation of wings to reduce embodied carbon over time

campus_buildings.name: Mercator I

visual.height: slim tower; a prominent mid-to-high rise relative to nearby low blocks, easily recognizable from Toernooiveld
colors: reflective blue/grey tint depending on light

bikes: Mercator bike racks mainly on the Huygens-facing side
traffic: visitors arriving by bike or on foot; occasional taxis for meetings

facilities: shared reception areas and small breakout lounges
sustainability: high-performance glazing typical for tech offices
bike-first access with limited surface parking

campus_buildings.name: Mercator II

visual.height: slim tower; sibling to Mercator I with similar overall proportion and corporate-tech aesthetic

bikes: overflow racks along the connecting paths
traffic: steady meeting traffic through the day

sustainability: emphasis on public transport and cycling connections

campus_buildings.name: Mercator III

visual.height: slim tower; part of the Mercator family with a contemporary high-tech look
colors: deep-toned frames with variable reflections in sunlight

greenery: rows of young trees along the approach

facilities: shared facilities with the other Mercator towers
people: project teams meeting with university groups

campus_buildings.name: Elinor Ostromgebouw

visual.height: mid-rise, clean rectangular; a composed series of modern blocks forming a cohesive academic complex
shapes: clear main entrance frontage with signage
unique: one building houses both sports centre and management faculty
big board/meeting rooms feel very spacious

greenery: rows of trees framing pedestrian approaches
bikes: spillover racks along the main path
traffic: sports traffic to the right side, management traffic to the left side
entrance level has an underpass area with many associations

sustainability: shading and efficient HVAC typical of modern faculty buildings

campus_buildings.name: Collegezalencomplex

shapes: broad steps and ramps to lobbies

bikes: extremely busy racks at peak hours
traffic: queues before large lectures and occasional written exams

facilities: central lecture location for many studies
occasional written exams (increasingly less, moved to Comenius)
people: large cohorts gathering between time slots
invigilators during the remaining exam moments

bikes: major bike parking between UB and Erasmus
SPAR next to the bike parking near Erasmus

facilities: Faculty of Philosophy, Theology and Religious Studies
direct indoor access from De Refter

traffic: evening study crowd during exam weeks
